basics.label: Lead Data Scientist
basics.name: Colin Middleton
basics.summary: Lead Data Scientist specializing in advanced analytics, statistical modeling, and AI product development to drive significant business impact. Proven ability to establish data science functions, partner with cross-functional stakeholders to align technical work with strategic priorities, and deliver quantified results that build organizational trust in data-driven decision-making. Adept at owning end-to-end analytical projects, developing innovative solutions for ambiguous problems, and leveraging Python and SQL for complex data analysis and model implementation.

projects.description: Collaborated with data providers and city government stakeholders to align on data strategy and present findings to the Spokane City Council.
highlights: Led training and evaluation of predictive models (Linear Regression, Cox Proportional Hazards, LSTM, Logistic Regression, ANN), achieving a peak AUC of 0.81 with Logistic Regression, demonstrating strong statistical analysis and AI/ML capabilities.
Addressed extreme class imbalance (0.39% positive class) via minority oversampling for robust model performance.
projects.name: Homelessness Prediction

publications.summary: Middleton, Colin D., et al. Plos one 18.10 (2023): e0292305. Showcasing expertise in predictive modeling and quantitative research.

skills.name: Programming Languages

highlights: Designed and built next-generation prediction models for bill routing grounded in contract structure, delivering more granular, explainable outputs that gave business stakeholders clear visibility into routing decisions and optimized operational efficiency.

Architected a modular codebase for model analysis pipelines, enabling flexible reuse across multiple use cases and significantly reducing the cost of future analyses, reflecting analytical thought leadership and infrastructure development.

Designed and built an ETL pipeline for savings prediction models, implementing robust handling of malformed data to ensure consistent, reliable model inputs at scale, critical for AI product reliability.

Led a cross-functional initiative to expand analytical capabilities, partnering with product and operations stakeholders to define requirements, align priorities, gather feedback, and drive adoption, demonstrating strong collaboration and ownership.

Architected an intelligent backlog prioritization framework that optimized resource allocation, enabling human reviewers to focus on highest-impact work items, addressing ambiguous problems with data-driven solutions.

Designed and built an end-to-end prediction system for a bill treatment product, covering model development, scoring, and output delivery — establishing a reusable foundation for future model work and owning project outcomes.
Led the effort to standardize and automate recurring analyses, reducing manual effort and enabling the team to scale output without proportional headcount growth, driving process improvements.
work.name: MedRisk

Led 50+ individualized growth analyses for strategic prospects, directly contributing to a 30% increase in client acquisition — establishing data science as a measurable driver of revenue growth and identifying new opportunities.
work.name: Pearl Health

highlights: Developed advanced forecasting and prediction models for client and prospect KPIs, leveraging statistical techniques including exponential smoothing, multivariate regression, and Theta modeling to support growth-oriented analytics for the client acquisition team.
